questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country and city had to be interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Because of covid, I felt a little alone in the beginning. There was no welcome events and all communication with the Erasmus office was digitally, so you had to just wait patiently for them contacting you with what to do next.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got information on what to do via email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I asked the other students at campus a lot. They were very sweet and helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing quality is very low but still expensive. Start getting an impression of the situation early, and be aware that it's dificult to get a short term lease. Most leases are 4 + 4 which means you're commited for 4 years!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to commute

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can do most online. Information aren't posted a long time in advance online. When registering for classes, I would recommend waiting untill classes have begun. You can register for classes until just before the exams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I asked the other students - they're familiar with the systems, and they speak Italian so they can ask for help if something isn't working properly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and ask the other students for help and advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took ma-level courses, because they were taught in English, and it wasn't a problem to keep up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's similar - lectures with some student participation. Exams were very different though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bristish Theatre Studies and Performances
Social Media for Environmental Communication
Representation and Image Theories
Intellectual and Cultural History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all my courses. Intellectual and Cultural History is super interesting if you'd like to know more about Italian history and Italian politics and culture. British Theatre Studies and Performances is a very cosy and chilled course. The professor is super sweet and the other students were very open and nice as well. You don't have to do much to keep up with the course and if you're a little interested in the arts, cultural, or theatrical scene of Milan, you will mostly just sit and talk about that and go to see plays together (also in English).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of money on food, but mostly when traveling and going out to dinner at night.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cheapest air bnbs around Italy are 40 eur a night, and if you hope to go to Rome, book in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really engage much with these, so I'm not entirely sure on the options available. I know the ESN arranged a lot of stuff, but I didn't participate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed traveling around Milan and exploring more of Italy. Especially going on one-day hiking trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See more of Italy! Milano is far from the nicest place in Italy, but it's well connected. It's a nice place to start exploring from.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: You have to be patient with a lot of things. Everything seems very unorganised from a Danish perspective and often things take longer or seem inefficient. Italians don't stress so try not to stress either.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are very nice and open but you might have to be the one who approach them and start the conversation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italian bureaucracy. Especially around exams. I found it helpful to just ask the locals and then do like them. And don't stress about it, often you can talk to the people in charge and work something out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: If you embrace it, it's super nice that many things are more relaxed. Trains and exams are difficult to figure out, but if you get it wrong or it takes you longer it's often not an issue. No one really has everything under control, so they don't expect you to have it either. Ask the locals for help.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't just stay in Milan, explore the country! It gets cold in winter and Milano is too hot in summer, so try to get out of the city. Be patient, and ask the students for help.
The best, local restaurants and (coffee) bars are not the most fancy looking but often the sleezy ones.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will probably be asked for your "codice fiscale". Don't bother applying for one, the process takes forever. If you search for "codice fiscale generator" online you can generate a fake one which will work just fine for most purposes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel around Italy and the food and coffee culture. I enjoyed the simple way of cooking with only a few ingredients, but ingredients of the highest, most tasty quality. I also really enjoyed eating late in evening, starting with a small pasta dish perhaps followed up by a pizza and dessert. I've also become slightly addicted to my after-lunch espresso.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did my exchange in my last semester of my bachelors which ment I was very busy also writing applications and planning what to do next. My biggest regret is not having more time to just enjoy Italy and explore Milano, instead of sitting inside working.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
